text:
Priya: Hey team — escalating an ongoing Private deployment issue for AcmeCorp. They see intermittent 500s and a spike in billing tokens after the 2026-03-15 runtime rollout. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (text) and /v1/embeddings. Customer supplied two sample request IDs: r-0a1b2c3d and r-9z8y7x6w. They also reported higher latency (p95 ~ 3.2s) right before the 500s. Javier (customer) ran a quick curl and attached logs. We need repro steps, a debug bundle from the collector, and guidance for redaction + upload.

Alex: Thanks Priya. Can you paste the curl they used and any short log excerpts? Also which Private flavor (VPC vs on-prem)?

Priya: On-prem (managed private bundle). Curl they used (redacted token):

```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.acme.redwood.local/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"owl-7b","input":"Summarize the Q1 report"}'
```

Response snippet they saw:

```
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "internal_server_error",
  "message": "runtime: kernel launch failed: CUDA out of memory",
  "request_id": "r-0a1b2c3d"
}
```

Priya: They also attached a small tail of the serving logs (again redacted customer info):

```
[2026-03-16T14:02:11Z] serving-runtime: request r-0a1b2c3d start seq=128
[2026-03-16T14:02:11Z] runtime-kernel: launch attempt failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
[2026-03-16T14:02:11Z] serving-runtime: fallback-to-cpu? false
[2026-03-16T14:02:11Z] serving-runtime: returning 500 to client
```

Sam: That looks like a KV-cache / batch-size OOM on GPU at the time of the request. Two things to gather ASAP:
- full collector debug bundle from the private node that served r-0a1b2c3d
- the runtime config used (batch limits, kv-cache size, quantization profile)

Sam: Priya — can we ask them to run the collector script below on the affected private host (this is the recommended, minimal step)? It will redact keys and attempt a presigned upload. Replace <SUPPORT_PRESIGN_URL> with the URL I'll DM to you.

```
sudo /opt/redwood/collector/debug-collector \
  --request-ids r-0a1b2c3d,r-9z8y7x6w \
  --include-logs /var/log/redwood/serving.log \
  --include-config /etc/redwood/runtime.yaml \
  --redact --redact-rules /etc/redwood/redact-rules.yml \
  --presign-url "<SUPPORT_PRESIGN_URL>" \
  --upload
```

Olivia: Note — older on-prem installs (pre-2026-01) require collector v0.9+ for automatic redaction. If their collector is older it will fail the `--redact` step. Priya, did they mention the collector binary version? Javier said they installed in Dec 2025; that might be v0.8.x.

Priya: Javier confirmed collector version looks like v0.8.4 from `/opt/redwood/collector/VERSION`. He tried `--redact` and got `unsupported-flag` error. He can update but they'd prefer not to reboot production nodes.

Alex: OK — two fallback options if they can't upgrade right away:
1) Run collector without `--redact` and upload via presigned URL; we will perform redaction on our side (requires presign to support server-side redact job) — I'll check if current support presign endpoint accepts non-redacted bundles.
2) If presign fails (network egress policies), instruct them to scp the bundle to our bastion at 10.33.5.12:/incoming/acme/ using a one-time key. We'll provide the steps.

Sam: For option 1, we need the debug bundle metadata to include the exact `/etc/redwood/runtime.yaml` and a copy of `serving.log` rotated last 5MB. Also request they capture `nvidia-smi` output at the time of trouble and `dmesg | tail -n 200` in case GPU OOMs show up at kernel level.

Priya: I'm going to ask Javier to run the collector without `--redact` and to attach these extra commands:

```
# nv output
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used,memory.total --format=csv

# kernel logs
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg_tail.txt
```

Priya: Javier ran the non-redacted collector attempt and the CLI failed at upload with a 403 from the presign endpoint. He pasted the upload debug below:

```
DEBUG: presign upload -> POST https://support-upload.redwood.com/presign
DEBUG: got 403 Forbidden
ERROR: upload failed: presign returned 403
bundle path: /tmp/debugbundle-acme-2113456789.tar.gz
```

Olivia: 403 from presign on an on-prem install often means the outgoing service account token expired or the presign URL whitelist is missing their IP. I'll ping infra to check the presign ACL for Acme's site.

deploy-bot: deploy: runtime-rollout v2026-03-15 applied to cluster acme-prod-1 at 2026-03-15T02:17:04Z

Alex: Good catch deploy-bot — correlates with their timeline. Olivia, can infra confirm whether the presign endpoint expects a signed agent JWT that may have rotated on 2026-03-10? If so, the collector won't be able to presign until they rotate the agent key.

Olivia: Confirmed: the org-level agent key rotated on 2026-03-10 and we have a migration window. If collector v0.8.4 doesn't fetch the new agent token, presign will 403. Two operational paths:
- They upgrade collector binary (safe, no reboot). I'll DM a hot patch script that replaces the collector binary in-place.
- Or we provide an SFTP fallback. I'll prepare a one-time scp key and path and post instructions.

Priya: I told Javier we can accept a direct scp to our bastion if they're blocked. He agreed to scp. Olivia, can you post the scp command and the one-time key TTL? Also Alex, once we have the bundle we'll run redaction and then look for the runtime trace around r-0a1b2c3d.

Olivia: One-time scp details (TTL 2 hours):

```
# on their side
scp /tmp/debugbundle-acme-2113456789.tar.gz support_uploader@10.33.5.12:/incoming/acme/

# we'll confirm receipt and then move to secure storage
```

Olivia: I've created an upload ticket and sent the private key via DM to Priya. Priya, please pass to Javier out-of-band.

Priya: Sent key to Javier. He confirmed upload complete at 2026-03-16T16:12:34Z. Bundle path received: s3://support-incoming/acme/debugbundle-acme-2113456789.tar.gz (we pulled it from the bastion).

Sam: I'll start redaction + analysis on the bundle. Quick pointers on what I'm checking:
- confirm model weights/quantization used
- check per-request batch size, max_tokens, and whether client sent `stream: true` (changes batching)
- look for contiguous OOM traces in dmesg/nvidia-smi
- verify if runtime attempted GPU->CPU fallback (should be false)

Sam: If it's an OOM due to a sudden large batch, we may recommend capping `max_batch_tokens` or enabling kv-cache trimming for that model, or suggesting a canary to a quantized variant.

Priya: Perfect. I'll update the customer with ETA ~2 business hours for initial triage and keep this thread updated. Marking as high-priority for billing impact.

Alex: Thanks everyone — post the analysis here once redaction is done and share any temporary mitigation we can push to the customer's runtime config (prefer non-disruptive runtime overrides). :thumbsup:
